title: POC scoping: benchmark harness integration - Acme Payments
next_steps: Jordan to share Redwood benchmark harness repo and runbook
Acme to provide sample production prompt set and 1 week of request traces
Schedule initial benchmark run (Redwood + Acme) for 2025-11-18
Priya to follow up on VPC peering requirements and sample load generator config
action_items: Jordan Kim - share benchmark harness repo, scripts, and README - due 2025-11-15
Samir Patel - export 7 days of request traces and sample prompts, anonymized - due 2025-11-14
Maya Ruiz - confirm network egress rules and provide account for test VPC - due 2025-11-16
Priya Desai - prepare baseline Redwood config (streaming + non-streaming) and expected metrics capture - due 2025-11-17
summary: POC scoping focused on integrating Acme's benchmark scripts with Redwood's harness. Reviewed success criteria (p95 latency, qps, error budget), workload sizing (concurrency, sequence length distribution), and streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs. Agreed on next steps: share harness, provide sample traces, schedule initial benchmark run, and validate VPC/access requirements.
questions: What are the p95/p99 latency targets for your checkout flow?
Do you plan to use streaming responses in production or batch non-streaming calls?
Any hard constraints on cost per 1k tokens or per-request cost?
Can you provide sample prompt distribution and typical sequence lengths?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to cover the benchmark harness integration and scope the POC. Quick intros?
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, CTO at Acme Payments. We care about latency for checkout flows and token cost.
[00:18] Maya Ruiz: Maya, SRE. I'll be owning VPC/networking and run infra for the tests.
[00:23] Samir Patel: Samir, ML Eng, I'll own the scripts and metrics.
[00:28] Priya Desai: Priya from Redwood, SE focused on performance, happy to dig into load profiles.
[00:33] Jordan Kim: Great. High level: we want to validate latency and throughput on representative traffic and show economic numbers. Today well align on success criteria, what scripts you have, and how we run streaming vs non-streaming.
[01:02] Samir: Quick note: our checkout path is latency sensitive, p95 target around 120-150 ms, p99 under 300 ms, that's our goal for auth/decision calls. We also have a background scoring job that's fine with higher latency.
[01:25] Priya: Cool, that's helpful. Two clarifications: those targets are network-to-network or server-only? Means including client telemetry?
[01:33] Liam: Ideally end-to-end, but for benchmarks we'll probably look at server-side p95 from Redwood to token completion. We can map back to end-to-end after.
[01:41] Priya: Understood. For the harness we need the sample prompt set and a distribution of sequence lengths. Also concurrency profile (steady qps vs spikes). Do you have traces?
[01:55] Samir: Yeah we can export 7 days of traces, anonymized. We'll include common prompt variants, typical token counts (mean ~110 tokens, tail to 600), and step-through variants.
[02:10] Jordan Kim: Perfect. On Redwood side our harness supports streaming and non-streaming modes. Streaming helps perceived latency but may change throughput due to more frequent socket writes and backpressure. For smaller responses streaming wins for user experience.
[02:28] Maya: We actually ship streaming to clients for the UX, but some internal services call non-streaming. We need to validate both.
[02:35] Priya: We'll run both modes during the POC. For streaming we measure first-byte latency and time-to-complete; for non-streaming we measure server completion p95/p99. We'll also capture CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates.
[02:50] Samir: How do you handle KV cache in the harness? Our production uses prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[02:58] Priya: We can simulate KV cache warm/warm-up states. The harness supports pre-populating KV with common prefixes. We'll run cold, warm, and hot cache experiments and report hit rates and token cost.
[03:15] Jordan Kim: Important for cost modelling: please tell us which prompts are highly repeated vs unique, that affects batching and cache value.
[03:24] Samir: We'll label the traces accordingly.
[03:28] Liam: On sizing: what's a realistic concurrency to hit for baseline? Our peak is about 120 tps (transactions per second) during peak sales, but those are mixed. For model calls, maybe 40-60 qps to the LLM for auth decisions.
[03:44] Priya: Ok we'll scale harness to test 10, 30, 60 qps and run spike tests to 120 qps to see graceful degradation. We'll measure error rates and tail latency.
[03:56] Maya: We'll need to ensure VPC peering and firewall rules allow our load generator to hit Redwood dedicated endpoints. Also if the POC uses Redwood Private, we might request an on-prem package demo.
[04:10] Jordan Kim: For the POC we typically do three lanes: hosted Redwood with the same model, Dedicated reserved pool if you want isolation, and a config that matches your prod infra. We can also run a Private trial but that requires infra lead time.
[04:24] Samir: We're most interested in Dedicated but want to start with hosted to iterate faster.
[04:29] Priya: That makes sense. We'll capture throughput and cost comparisons for hosted vs Dedicated and show per-1k-token cost estimates. Expect quantization/quant profiles to affect speed/cost; we'll run MMAP vs int8-ish configs.
[04:45] Liam: On timelines, wed like a first run within this week or next. Can you turn the harness up quickly?
[04:53] Jordan Kim: We can share the harness repo today; Priya can stand up baseline configs and we can run a first smoke test by 2025-11-18. Full runs (different cache states, streaming/non-streaming, qps sweep) will take a few days.
[05:06] Maya: Are there any agents or connectors we need to install on our side?
[05:10] Priya: No agents required. We provide a load generator example using k6 and a Python harness that hits the Redwood API. For VPC tests we'll provide Terraform snippets and an example peering config.
[05:21] Samir: How do we measure cost? Do you provide token counts and GPU time per request?
[05:25] Jordan Kim: Yes the harness emits per-request token counts, GPU utilization, and we can map into cost model for hosted and Dedicated. We'll give CSVs and a dashboard.
[05:33] Samir: Nice. For streaming vs non-streaming what are the main tradeoffs we should expect?
[05:38] Priya: Streaming reduces time-to-first-byte and improves UX, but increases per-connection overhead and can reduce overall throughput depending on network and client behavior. Non-streaming has simpler backpressure and often better batching efficiency, so could be cheaper at high QPS. We'll quantify both in the POC.
[05:54] Liam: Any gotchas re: our tokens per request distribution - long tails will kill p99 right?
[05:59] Priya: Exactly. We'll surface token distribution impact and suggest prefix truncation or guardrails. Also recommend batching windows and KV cache tuning to reduce repeated compute.
[06:12] Jordan Kim: Security questions: Samir wanted to confirm audit logs, KMS/HSM options, and SOC 2.
[06:18] Samir: Yes we'll need to capture logs for compliance and verify retention options.
[06:22] Priya: Redwood provides request-level audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and we have SOC 2 Type II. We'll send the security pack and a shorter security one-pager for your compliance team.
[06:34] Maya: We'll need an IP allowlist and SAML/SSO for the console access.
[06:38] Jordan Kim: We'll include SAML SSO setup doc and console RBAC notes.
[06:43] Priya: Back to benchmarks - expected deliverables: CSVs of latency/throughput, GPU/CPU utilization traces, token cost estimates, and a short analysis noting where p95/p99 regressions happen relative to your targets.
[06:57] Samir: Sounds good. Also include scenario where KV cache warms gradually over 24 hours, we want to see steady state.
[07:05] Priya: Will do. We'll run cold->warm->hot runs.
[07:09] Jordan Kim: Ok let's recap actions and timeline. We'll send the harness repo and runbook today, Samir will provide traces by Friday (2025-11-14), Maya will confirm VPC details by 2025-11-16, and Priya will schedule the initial benchmark run w/ Acme for 2025-11-18. Full report follow-up early the week after.
[07:30] Liam: Good, that's aligned.
[07:33] Jordan Kim: Any other questions?
[07:35] Maya: One question on metrics retention - how long do you keep raw traces?
[07:39] Priya: Default retention is 30 days for detailed traces; we can extend for POC on request. We'll note that in the runbook.
[07:45] Jordan Kim: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the repo link and meeting notes.
[07:51] Liam: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:53] END TRANSCRIPT
